title: Do I need another COVID shot to complete the series or am I fully vaccinated?
selftext:
47F, 5'4", 150#, white, non-smoker, no medical issues, no current medications,  California, USA. Duration of complaint (so question not removed) :4 months. I caught COVID in September after I had my first vaccine. I received the remdesivir therapy, and was advised that I could get another vaccine in 90 days.

I went at 90 days and got another vaccine, and was told by the pharmacist that I'm fully vaccinated. This doesn't seem right to me. I'm a veterinarian, and my understanding is that vaccines need to be given at 3-4 week intervals. If one is missed then the series needs to be restarted from the beginning.

I was thinking I should get another vaccine 4 weeks after the one I got at 90 days post-remdesivir. Does anyone know what the protocol is? Thanks in advance

title: Infant COVID-19 Risk w/ Unvaccinated Family Members
selftext:
My wife and I are vaccinated and boostered. We have a six-month old son and have been planning for several months to attend Christmas in Northern Indiana with my family (we live on the West Coast).  About half of my family is anti-vaccination and they have been operating without restrictions for a long time now. When we bought our tickets, cases were low and we figured that with low risk to children, this Christmas would be the time to accept the situation and reconnect with everyone.

Currently, however, Indiana is in the midst of a massive COVID spike. We asked our pediatrician for advice on this trip and she recommended against it, citing some indication of special problems (concerning chest xrays) for children under age one and some "concerning early data" on Omicron. She also said that vaccine authorization for 6 months+ is likely in the next 2-3 months and asked if we could wait until then. We got a second opinion from another pediatrician (family friend) and this doctor said the chances of anything really bad happening to our baby are extremely low and that attending is not clearly a wrong decision.

We are not sure what to do. Speaking with the family about a potential middle ground of us flying in but not attending the main gatherings and not staying with my parents (who are 70 and unboostered 8 months after J&J) made it clear that it would be better for everyone if we simply postponed rather than arrive and stay distanced. The family gathering is likely to be about 25 people, mix of adults and kids over 5, in a very tight environment.

Not attending is clearly the safest option but at this point we are also concerned about negative effects on family relationships. This may be the only chance most family members have to see the baby while he is still really a baby. In some ways this situation feels like two types of irrationality (us worried about extremely low chances of something happening to our child, and family members worried about some theoretical vaccine risk).

We are trying to untangle this risk and looking for any input or further perspective that will help us make the stay/go decision. Thank you!

title: Reddit, should I be concerned?
selftext:
I know damn well that a lot of people - especially teenagers my age - tend to question their health, rely on diagnoses, and overthink, but I'd appreciate some feedback. I know it's long, but please please please help if you can. 

( If you don't want to read it, at least click on the link and listen to the video of my mouth. It'll freak you out. Luv u ♥️ )

I'm a 16 year old female. I'm 5'5 and weigh about 105 pounds. I'm half Filipino(mom) and half American(dad). My mom is of latino descent. I usually take 60mg of Dextroamphetamine(Adderall XR) in the morning, 1mg of Prazosin(Minipress) at night, birth control, and Sertraline(Zoloft). I'm not sure if this is relevant, but heart, lung, sleep, and brain problems are very common in both sides of my family. My dad actually had a brain tumor that hemorrhaged, which is cool. (Dad, if you see this, hi! Get off Reddit and hug me, damn it.)

Anyways, my main concerns are my excessive sleepiness and shortness of breath. Now, I know what you're probably thinking. 

A teenager? Tired? How UNIQUE and CONCERNING! 

It's a bit more than that, though. I'm SO TIRED. 
But this is fairly recent. And it's getting worse. I just kinda want some tips and coping mechanisms with my excessive sleepiness, though, so if you don't care about that please skip to my shortness of breath paragraph. I just hope that my tiredness isn't related to my heart or lungs or anything.


Short backstory: Last September, I underwent a very traumatic event and was raped. The trauma really didn't end there, though. It dragged on until June 2018 due to  constant harassment and threats. From September - December 2017, i rarely slept. I'm talking about a ridiculously small amount of sleep - around 2 hours worth every 3 or 4 days. During this period of temporary insomnia, I was having intense hallucinations and was going to counseling for my PTSD. At some point, though, my body had had enough sleep deprivation, and I was unable to stay awake for ANYTHING. I was then prescribed Prazosin, Sertraline, and Adderall. I was thought to potentially have narcolepsy, since it runs in my dad's family. Since then, I've struggled with extreme fatigue and tiredness.

Today I recieved my sleep study and polysomnogram results, which were not consistent with narcolepsy. I DO have an incredibly fast sleep onset, though, and can sleep within 2 minutes. This was relieving but has me wondering if my excessive sleepiness is trauma induced. Can anyone conclude this? Besides managing a sleep schedule, how do I combat my sleepiness? Is this normal? I've fallen asleep driving(while stopped in traffic), in every class hour almost every day, while talking, eating, typing, walking, etc. I have constant sleepwalking and talking episodes, but my PSG showed no REM abnormalities. My dad wants to lower my adderall dosage, but I'm barely managing on 60mg. I don't know how to begin to convey my tiredness. I have cataplexy-like episodes of muscle weakness and fatigue when stressed or physically exerted, and fall asleep almost immediately after. Ultimately I'm mainly concerned about my grades, safety, and presentation since I'm always drowsy. I just want to cope and not have it interfere with my daily life. I usually sleep at about 10:30pm and wake up at 7, but I'm often exhausted and sleep even earlier. :( However, I nap a lot during the day and try to avoid napping past 4. It's probably just how I deal with stress, but the sleepiness itself stresses me out even more. What else can I even do? At least if I had narcolepsy I'd have solid answers. The best advice they had for me was to correct my sleeping schedule, but I shit you not I've slept for days and still felt uncontrollably tired.  It's very frustrating to sleep through things I don't want to miss. It's very frustrating to know I can dismiss puzzle alarms in my sleep. It's frustrating to know that when I sleep talk I say things I don't mean. My dad punched a hole in my door because I was conversing with him while asleep, lmao. I don't even know what I want anymore. 


NOW FOR MY NEXT AND MORE IMPORTANT CONCERN! 

 It's actually more important than the sleepiness, so sorry for the long paragraphs. 

Short backstory: When I was 8, I used an inhaler as needed because i lived in SLC and the smog was terrible. I didn't use it much at all though. 

I moved to a different place in Utah without smog in January 2017 and completely forgot about my inhaler.

 However, since about March I've become increasingly fatigued and out of breath. It's gotten really bad lately and I was prescribed my inhaler again. It doesn't help much. At all. My peak flow chart does increase, though... My doctor doesn't know if it's asthma or not.

I wouldn't be too concerned except I've also developed an externally audible heartbeat in my mouth. I can't stand up or roll over without wheezing, and my heartbeat is very fast. My muscles become weak and I almost collapse if I don't catch my breath. It is audible when my mouth is closed, but it is a lot louder when my mouth is open. In a silent room, you can hear it from about 5 feet away. This happens with any exertion, all day, every day. The heartbeat thing started in June or July. Since then, my muscle weakness and shortness of breath have been worse than ever. 

Here is a video of my heartbeat!
 https://photos.app.goo.gl/qFaxrHAhWpNZXwxf7 

Ignore my disgusting mouth. I have other recordings, but this one's the clearest and it's easiest to see that it's in conjunction with my heart. 

This also interferes with my daily life. It sucks! I've had an EKG done a few months ago with no major concerns, and my lungs sound normal on a stethoscope. 

My adderall makes it a bit worse, but my heartbeat thing, weakness, and shortness of breath happens even without it. Same with the Prazosin and sertraline and birth control. I can't walk to one class to another without being late because I constantly have to catch my breath. :( I don't know how to combat this either. Is it something I should be concerned about? Because I'm kinda concerned. I just don't know what to do about it, since my inhaler doesn't help me much. Anyone have an explanation to what the hell the sound is? My lungs? My heart? It's probably nothing, but that coupled with muscle weakness, chest pain, and fatigue is enough to convince me it might be something else.  

What do y'all think? Should I be doing anything to treat this? Does anyone know what it is? Is it normal? Should I be watching out for anything? I don't know, I'm probably paranoid. It's just weird. And uncomfortable. I hate being so aware of my heart.

 I like freaking people out with my mouth, but at the end of the day, it freaks me out the most. I dunno. Any feedback would be cool, even if it's just "wtf ur heart sounds like 2 dudes banging." 

this probably didn't make much sense because i was half asleep writing some of this but yeah

TL,DR;
im very very very tired and dont know how to deal with it, and ive ruled out narcolepsy. i think it's trauma induced. i also am very weak and cant breathe a lot. and i hear my heart in my mouth and it is very loud

title: Short seizure after orgasm and hard sex
selftext:
36F, 5'3", 110lbs, white/caucasian, U.S. West. On birth control since June.

Hi, I'm writing this together with my partner. She experienced what could best be described as a very short seizure. We're concerned about what could be the cause and what we can do to help.

We woke up together, immediately started having sex, she had an orgasm in the doggy style position, and we continued having vigorous sex for a couple of minutes in the same position. We paused, she raised and turned her head back to kiss me, i put my hand lightly around her throat, we kissed, but then she started biting down on my tongue. I panicked, yelled, and pulled her off. She fell forward and shook in what looked to me like a seizure for around 3 seconds. Her eyes were open, her mouth was open but seemed clenched, and her body was convulsing as if in a seizure.

In her words: I came to feeling my body shaking and feeling confused about what was happening. I didn't know what the last thing we did was or how much time had passed. It felt like I had had a quick dream and was shaking for some reason. My partner said to me, "Ow, you just bit my tongue really hard!" and I said, "We were kissing still?" I lost time and control of my body, so he filled me on what happened. The rest of the day I felt a little tired but fine.

I went to the doctor that afternoon, told her I lost consciousness, and described what my partner said happened. She then tested my pulse and blood pressure in a laying down position, sitting, and standing, but all were normal. She asked if I had had anything to do drink, and I said that I had had a couple cocktails the night before. She didn't seem concerned. She asked about cannabis, and I said that I had smoked the night before and did a few times a week. My doctor wasn't sure if it was fainting or a seizure, but said that usually with fainting you know when it's about to happen (and I agree, that's been the case for me when I've fainted twice before). But she said that seizures usually last at least a minute. I don't have a past of seizures and I'm healthy overall, so she wanted to consult with the neurology department. She then had me get an EKG, even though she didn't think it was because of my heart. I got some blood work done and am waiting for the results. My doctor also ordered a brain MRI and an EEG, which I will do soon. In the meantime, I'm not allowed to drive until we figure out what happened, or until a few months pass.

We're curious about what could have happened, if it could have been related to orgasm or rough sex, and if there are any triggers to avoid in the future. Have any of the doctors here seen this happen before? Is my doctor doing the right thing? I'm pretty upset that I can't drive for a while, even though this episode lasted for about 5 seconds.

title: Stung and in severe pain 4 hours later
selftext:
26 year old Caucasian female, located in Texas. 

I've never been stung by anything before, whether it be a bee, wasp, etc. Tonight was my lucky night to finally experience a sting, and of course it had to be a yellowjacket/hornet. I am not sure which it was, I know they look similar. The sting itself was painful but nothing compared to the pain I've been experiencing for the past four hours. 

I was stung in a toe on my left foot. It's like a very severe, intense burning. Excruciating waves will hit the toe and make my left leg involuntarily twitch/tremble. I can't put pressure on the toe at all, and can't really walk on the foot without being very uncomfortable.  

I took a credit card and scraped for a stinger but never found one. There was a small dot of blood on my toe where I think I was stung. I took Tylenol, it didn't help. I've been putting ice on it and switching on and off every ten minutes. Toward the end of the ten minutes when the ice is om my toe, it feels great because well, my toe is numb. A couple minutes after I remove the ice, the raging pain comes back. 

At this point, I can't sleep and I'm starting to be concerned. Like I said, I've never been stung so I have no idea what to expect. Should the pain have settled by now? Should I go to urgent doc if it still hurts in the morning?

title: Should I worry about a non-punctured cat bite? Is rabies possible?
selftext:
Help me out here reddit. I 19M, is currently taking care of my neighbors dogs and their cat while they are on vacation for a week. I don't know a whole lot about the cat other than that it "adopted" the family, which probably means they started feeding a stray. While they are away, it sleeps and stays in the garage. Anyway, this cat sort of bit me. I was petting it and it wrapped its paws around my hand and put its teeth onto my hand but it DID NOT leave a puncture wound/it didn't break the skin I don't think... if it did it the mark must be really really small. This "incident" happend three or four days ago and the cat is acting normal as a cat would act. I pretty sure it's been eating, drinking water, it rubs up against my leg somtimes if i get close, not acting aggressive, etc.

My main concern is as you might have guessed from the title: rabies. I researched it a little bit and know about its deadliness if not treated and some of the warning signs if an animal has rabies but thats about it.

title: How do I give a thank you gift?
selftext:
My GP at my school is the best doctor that I’ve had and probably will ever have. I’ve been seeing this doctor for two years and she is very understanding, listens, explains, and answers any questions that I have (even though they are very very specific questions) or admits she don’t know the answer if she actually don’t know instead of talking just to fill up an answer. title: Disordered eating caused by medication
selftext:
Age: 31

Sex: F

Height: 5'6"

Weight: 137

Race: White

Duration of complaint: 9 months

Location: Texas / Stomach

Any existing relevant medical issues: Bipolar 2

Current medications: Lamictal 200mg

~~~

I've spent the last 12 months starting and discontinuing medications to treat recently-diagnosed bipolar disorder.  Depakote, Lexapro, Lamictal, Pristiq.  About 6 weeks ago, I quit Pristiq abruptly because it made me feel passively suicidal and completely apathetic, and my eating habits have gotten worse.  I have not been to a doctor for a while and I'm waiting until my insurance kicks in in January, but even then I don't want to go back to my GP except for a Lamictal refill.  It's going to be a financially-stressful year.

Lamictal has been good for stabilizing, and it's helped me effortlessly cut my worst habit: alcohol abuse (and, randomly, lifelong nail-biting), but it also destroyed my appetite.

In the last few months, I've added strength training to a casual cardio routine (stationary cycling, running, 4-5 times a week), and was getting to a comfortable and healthy weight for my height and frame.  The weight lifting helped with appetite somewhat, and I found myself eating two decent meals a day without a struggle.  Felt pretty good with where I was.  That's when I quit Pristiq.

Now I don't get hungry.  My stomach hurts and I get weak (actually fainted a few days ago at an exercise class), but it doesn't read as hunger.  I hate eating with people, being "forced" to eat dinner with others during the holidays.  I stopped eating meat back in the spring, mostly because that's an easy excuse to choose/provide my own, lighter meal.  My stomach hurts when I eat a regular-sized portion and I use that an excuse to skip more meals.

I'm not underweight (though I'm probably losing some muscle mass lately).  I occasionally binge on sweet things, then feel terrible afterwards.  I have lost a lot of weight this year (~30 pounds), which was initially a good thing, but people have started to tell me it's enough.

My med student friend says I'm going to have problems if I keep this up... which I didn't really need him to tell me, but I don't know how to get back into a normal routine again.

I ate a cup of plain, whole-fat yogurt this morning.  I'll have a salad for lunch because I know I need vitamins.  I'm trying to save room for a holiday get-together tonight, but I'm probably going to have a problem with the rich food there.  

What are some steps I can take to climb out of this hole?

Thanks.

title: Presented to the ER in afib w/rvr. Resting HR 200bpm. Cardioversion returned sinus rhythm and normal resting HR. A bunch of tests later, cardiologist isn't concerned but I am having major doubts and am pretty scared. I don't trust my cardiologist (I can explain why) what should I do?
selftext:
A year ago I was having very bad gastrointestinal issues, I had an ulcer in my stomach (confirmed with endoscopy). When my stomach would hurt badly, my heart would race, and I would sometimes go into afib. One morning the afib was worse than usual, and I went to the ER and my heart got up to 200bpm and they had to cardiovert me. They sent me home on Flecainide.

An echocardiogram, 30-day event monitor, and blood tests later my cardiologist isn't concerned. Threw me on Metoprolol 50mg daily to control the heart rate and told me afib isn't cureable. I only go into afib when my stomach gets upset, so I asked him about vagal afib and he said it's not really a real thing. He really has never given me the time of day and his nurse practitioner is very rude as well. His office double books appointment times, and he is always in a huge rush when I see him. I can't ever ask him questions like "is this reversible?", "will I get blood clots and get strokes later in life?", "can I exercise?", etc etc. I tried to slow him down last time I saw him and said "I have some questions" and I got one question out and as he was answering the question he opened the door and started stepping out into the hallway - he answered my question then said "I'll see you in 6 months take care" and closed the door. I'm a shy person at doctors offices so I didn't protest, and I am too polite to just keep rattling off questions or stop him, he is the opposite he's a "speak up or I'm walking out the door" kind of guy, which I can respect but I need some patience here.

This has changed my entire life, I took this event extremally seriously. I quit drinking entirely, lost 100 freaking pounds over the last year (I was extremally obese). I am now trying to finish up my progress and start exercising, and I have two vacations coming up in a month and I want to know if I'm healthy enough to have a few glasses of wine or beers with friends while I'm on vacation - but he doesn't have the time of day for me.

I called his office today, for the first time ever I really don't bother them, left a message with his nurse practitioner and said "Hey, I've been trying to go jogging, but I keep going into afib while jogging and my stomach gets really upset, also my heart rate is 170bpm while I jog is this ok??" and she called back and just said "yup you're fine".

I lack confidence in these answers - I have so many questions and concerns in my head that I really want to get out like "how serious is this?", "why did I go into rvr and svt that one day?", "what can I do to never have to get cardioverted again?", "how many years might I have had afib before this without knowing it?", "have I had afib for so long that clots may have started to form?", "Is this afib just related to my weight and my gastrointestinal issues and it will go away as I keep losing weight?", "Will this continue forever? Will I need an ablation by the time I'm 40?", "Will I be on metoprolol for the rest of my life?", "Can I drink socially a few times a year?", "Can I take prescription pills like Adderall or Wellbutrin?", "What about other stimulants like caffeine?", "can I test my LHL and apo B? I was a fat pos for 10 years do I need to worry about atherosclerosis?". I need like a solid fuckin 15-20 minutes with this guy I just want to clear my head and feel ok about what's going on. If I have afib forever ok, I can accept that, but just sit me down for a few minutes and explain that I'm not gonna go back into SVT or RVR or have to get cardioverted ever again if I follow some rules. Getting cardioverted was a little traumatic I was fully awake and everything I will do anything to not have to go through that again.

Any advice is extremally appreciated, really stressed about all this over the past year. Thank you so much for your time and for reading.

title: How quickly does benzo addiction cause dependence?
selftext:
[Follow-up from my ER visit for detox:](https://old.reddit.com/r/AskDocs/comments/lzxjm5/went_to_the_er_yesterday_morning_for_alcohol/)

29-year-old male, 180 lbs, California.  I wrote a post about 10 days ago about my ER visit for alcohol withdrawal/help quitting and how I was released and, others than the ~140 AST/ALT and 2 BUN level I was relatively healthy.  Still 13 days sober.

The neuropathy is almost gone, although I still find I sometimes find myself leaning, like almost pigeon-toed, which I correct rather quickly.  Also it seems like the strength in my lower legs and calves are still not 100%, but they're getting better.

Overall, things are going very well and I'm the most productive I've been in years.

Starting on 3/6//10, I started using the stash of 10mg Valium that I had stashed up over 4 months (#120).  It was mostly to manage the shaky hands, anxiety, general sweatiness -- the usual.  I was taking it as prescribed, 3 times a day, but sometimes I'd take an extra one due to the severity of the symptoms.  This happened pretty regularly over that week, so taking 10mg Valium 4 times a day.

It felt so good for the chronic back pain I was having that finally was able to be relieved -- I can definitely understand how chronically hurt get people get so easily addicted to opiates now. ) I still don't if I was justifying the alcohol withdrawal symptoms, since I've heard it takes around 5 days of Valium/Librium to start making you feel "normal", although it was already a week at that point.

This next week was filled with increased dosages and taking them casually, even without the anxiety or back pain really.

So in total, I had #120 10mg valium in 14 days.  I talked to my PCP over the phone and was dishonest with her at first regarding the ER visit-- but she had my ER record so knew what I was really in there for.  She is giving my #13 tablets to last over the weekend, then probably put me on Librium.  

Does this length of binge use normally lead to withdrawals/dependency?

title: I went down the Chronic Lyme path, because I don’t know where else to go. Is there another path?
selftext:
This will all be in relation to my husband.

Caucasian
Male
33 years old

March 2020, Husband has taken up trail running, we live in western Montana. After pushing himself a little too hard on a run, he came home complaining of right leg IT band pain. Repeatedly came back even after refraining from any running for a month and a half and starting back very slowly. Also experienced foot pain that he attributed to plantar fasciitis. but he has very flat feet and an old ankle injury from a motorcycle wreck so I don’t know if that is relevant.

May 2020: he comes to me with what had been a VERY engorged tick that had been in his beard for roughly 3 days after an overnight backpacking trip. I urge him to see a doctor but he does not. The spot develops a large, sensitive lump that was warm to the touch and swollen for a while. A knot remained in the spot for several weeks. He continues his running, and soon develops pain is his left leg IT band. Foot pain is still very persistent and bad. By June 2020 he has developed hip pain in both hips and cannot continue running due to the multitude of issues. We are very outdoorsy people and most anything we did came with a ton of pain as the consequence. 

Fast forward to December 2020: he has seen his primary doctor who noted there seemed to be inflammation in his connective tissues but not his joints directly. He begins six (maybe eight I don’t remember) weeks of physical therapy. The IT band pain has migrated to the back of his knees (his hamstring connectors) and PT attributed this to his glutes not being engaged properly. There was zero improvement after PT. 

Our timeline gets blurry after this, but pain migrates from hamstring connectors, to groin, to elbows, he has bouts of carpal tunnel… he would always note that it wasn’t joint pain it was tissue pain. I sent him to an orthopedist for his hips thinking he had an impingement. They said nothing was wrong and his hips looked great. Primary doc sends him to a rheumatologist in Feb 2021. Tests for RA, Schogrens, ankylosis spondylitis, Ehlers Danos, and a few other things that are ruled out. He leaves with a vague diagnosis of hyper mobility with no follow up from the rheumatologist or primary doc. 

From Feb through July he basically just suffers. Nothing helps alleviate the connective tissue pain, activity makes it worse. By July I have discovered the path of Lyme disease. We visit a naturopath Lyme literate doctor who runs a very basic spot test for borrelia and bartonella. Both negative but he treats based on clinical diagnosis. At no point were we pressured or told to do anything we were not comfortable with. He is on the normal amount of Doxycycline that is normally used for Lyme along with azithromycin for four months and spent one month on Malarone for babesia but was taken off of it by naturopath because of liver enzyme levels. Naturopath stops all antibiotics and says he does not believe this can be attributed to Lyme and that the lack of reaction or real improvement suggests he does not have Lyme. The joint pain and bottom of foot pain persists and worsens after stopping antibiotics and remains bad even now, with intermittent days of feeling ok. Some days the hips are awful, today specifically his feet are killing him. 

He has also developed digestive issues in the last two months. It started with small amounts of food making him feel disgustingly full. Progressed to constant burping even after not eating for 14+ hours. There is no constipation or diarrhea but he describes his stomach as constantly feeling “blech” like it would when you have a massive hangover. There is no vomiting. He had a gallbladder attack about a month ago where it was twinging with worsening pain for about 24 hours. The feeling passed but he still had an ultrasound done which showed no stones or sludge and his liver and kidney looked fine. This was done at our local hospital and they reported nothing of concern. He does not eat consistently because the moment he does he feels gross. 

So here we are. Connective tissue pain has never resolved, has actually worsened. He has developed digestive issues and had problems with his gallbladder. His mental state has changed from a very level headed and calm person to an irritable and depressed person. He has a lot of memory issues and forgets names and words often. 

He is 5’8” weighing around 151 lbs, was lifting weights and working out up until he became unable to eat a lot due to these digestive issues and knew he wasn’t taking in enough calories. The man is always hydrated, true r/hydrohomies member. The weight lifting had to be restricted to upper body because the leg workouts affected his knees too badly. His elbows would hurt occasionally and he did develop more issues with his hands. His dad was an Olympic weight lifter and owned a gym so I am confident in his form and routine being good. 

His blood tests show very elevated eosinophils, slightly elevated liver enzymes, and normal thyroid levels. Stool test showed no parasites and celiac was negative. H. Pylori was negative. ANA, CRP and fecal calprotectin were normal.  

So where do we go from here? I have taken him off all supplements I had from the chronic Lyme community. He took Pepcid AC and his stomach felt normal for two days, we eliminated red meat which helped his stomach for about a week. Both stopped helping. Chronic Lyme and co infections felt like an answer but I see the science saying it’s not. We need a different path before we crumble. So what do you see?

title: Dermatology - Skin/Acne Breakouts
selftext:
Age: 24

Sex: Male

Height: 5'7"

Weight: 180.6 lbs

============

So I started working out about 3-4 weeks ago, mostly doing cardio and some weight training. I have not really worked out consistently or much for a very long time, so my body has increased a lot of sweat over the past few weeks from this activity. However, about a week ago, I noticed my neck has some bumps, and I knew exactly what they were.

Every morning I'd go to the gym, do 30+ mins of cardio, some dumbbell work, come home, and take a warm/hot shower. I love the feeling of a hot shower of course, especially the way it feels on your skin.

However, the neck bumps got redder, and then I found myself itching myself all over my body. First it was my thighs, then under my knees/calves, armpit area (both sides). All of a sudden acne spread to literally all parts of my body, including my face too.

This has happened before, primarily due to the heat & sun (I live in Arizona). And I've gotten heat rashes before. However, the last time this happened was back in early August, since then, it never happened. And it's super cold right now and there's barely any extreme sun, so why suddenly did this happen?

I'm trying to see a dermatologist but they're super booked so I'm here to get some perspective & insights. This has happened before and it's taken about 2 weeks to heal so I know it'll be fine, but I want to find out the root cause.

I think it might be a combination of things:

\- Not properly lathering body wash soap all over, causing dead skin cells and since I'm sweating a lot, it may be blocking the pores.

\- I realized I have been barely drinking water throughout the day. I only drink a lot of water during my exercises, then I drink a cup of tea, I eat a salad (Cucumbers, Tomatoes, Carrots), and then that's it. Barely much water throughout the day.

\- The hot showers may also have contributed.

Thoughts?

title: Mid-right side reducible abdominal bulge when I flex abdominal muscles?
selftext:
I've been concerned about a developing condition for almost two months now. I have had a few appointments to see my doctor, two sets of blood panels, and two ultrasounds performed attempting to diagnose this issue. 

Stats:
27yo
Male
5'9
215lb
Caucasian 
Colorado, mid height right side of abdomen
~2mo duration
Excessive alcohol use, chewing tobacco
Meds: occasional diphenhydramine, ibuprofen 

History:
It started in early November, about seven weeks ago, with a sharp pain in my upper right internal abdomen, right about where I think my diaphragm is located. In certain positions (bending over or leaning while standing), it felt like I had the wind knocked out of me. Pain would cause me to catch my breath. This lasted a few days. Then, once the pain stage subsided for the most part, I noticed a bulge on my right side at about navel height would appear when I flexed my abdominal muscles. The bulge was most prominent not directly in front or directly to the side; it's located about where my right nipple would be if it were at navel-height. When I flex, I feel the bulge internally as well. Currently, I have mild to moderate discomfort (not quite what I'd call pain) when coughing, twisting my torso, lifting heavy objects, and bending over. 

Steps taken so far:
Physical examination by PCP: inconclusive. Doctor doesn't think it's liver related. Said bulge is lower than liver, more concurrent with bowel. 

Blood panels: all normal except slightly elevated calcium, borderline elevated cholesterol, and significantly elevated fasting triglycerides. 

Imaging: 2 ultrasounds performed. First was looking for herniated abdominal wall. No evidence of localized hernia. Second was upper abdominal. Looked at liver, stomach, etc. Radiologist noted nothing abnormal. Liver not enlarged, no distinct masses visible. 

Current status: I've reduced alcohol consumption significantly, eating more fiber/veggies, eating less in general. The reducible bulge has not subsided. If anything it has gotten slightly larger, and may have moved/spread ventrally toward navel. 

My next step, according to the PCP, would be to get a CT scan if the symptom does not resolve itself. I'd prefer to avoid that if I can. So, I ask you all:

Have you seen anything similar to this, and if so, what did it turn out to be? Can you suggest a direction for me to head going forward? Should I seek advice from a gastroenterologist, an internal medicine doctor, or some other specialist? Would the CT scan be wise, or could perhaps a colonoscopy help in diagnosis of a possible bowel issue?

As of now, doc says I'm just supposed to "keep an eye on it" and report back if it worsens significantly. 

I'd appreciate any insight I can get. Thank you all!

title: I have been to several doctors and have not received any answers.
selftext:
I am a white male age 26, 5'10" 220 pounds located in Southern California.  The only current medication that I am on is finasteride which I have been on for years.  The only previous long term condition I have had is asthma.  

  
I need to preface this by saying that for the past two years I have felt that at certain moments my heart has constricted harder when beating.  This was scattered and typically occurred at night while I was in bed.  In June of this year I got some sort of infection and had a really bad sore throat the worst I've ever had.  I saw a doctor who gave me antibiotics, but this did not fully clear the infection and I had to return.  I saw another doctor who gave me stronger antibiotics and prednisone.  In addition to these they gave me a steroid shot and antibiotic shot.  The first noticeable instance came 30 minutes after receiving the shots.  I had a mild discomfort in my chest which persisted.  The following days the discomfort became stronger.  Approximately a week after receiving the shot I had an episode where I was seated at rest and had a hot flash, got very dizzy, it got hard to breath, the pain in my chest intensified, I started sweating, and my heart rate shot to 180.  (The heart rate was confirmed by an at home Pulsox monitor)  I called 911 and spent the night in the hospital.  My heart rate stabilized and went back down after the paramedics put an IV into my arm.  I was told by the doctor at the hospital "Whatever it was, we missed it." and was directed to go to my insurance networks hospital because they would have my records.  The following day I went and received a barrage of tests, all kinds of blood, urine, and x-rays of my chest.  Before being discharged I was told by the doctor that they believed that it might be pericarditis, but did not receive an official diagnosis.  I was given ibuprofen and told to take it easy for a few weeks.  

I followed the instructions and the pain did get better, but the odd feelings, discomfort. and palpitations did not.  Heart palpitations became more and more common and I started experiencing additional symptoms.  I could no longer sleep on my left side.  It felt like there was pooling pressure on my heart that would start building as soon as I laid down.  I could almost fall asleep but right before that happened I would shoot awake and my heart rate would skyrocket from the 60s to 120-130.  This eventually started happening while laying down on the right side as well and recently while laying on my back at an elevation.  In addition to this I have begun having issues with my stomach.  I have no nausea but I have discomfort in my stomach at all times.  This worsens after eating.  Heart palpitations have become an everyday occurrence.  Sometimes during the morning or afternoon, but everyday starting around 5-7 I get them intensely lasting until I fall asleep.  Again this worsens after eating.  This has been worsening and now in addition to the palpitations I have what I can only describe as vibrations in my chest and stomach area that accompany the palpitations.  My pulse starts feeling very intense in my neck. stomach, and the back of my thigh.  You can see these parts of my body move with the pulse.  My blood pressure also will rise going from normal ranges to stage 1 hypertension during these hours.  In addition to this every couple of days starting at the same time I get terrible bouts of anxiety.  In the past I have seen therapists for anxiety and taken pills from a psychiatrist, but this is the worst it's ever been.  I have never felt it like this before.  Strong feelings of dread and terror.

Other things have been happening more frequently than in the past, but not daily like the above.  I am not sure if these are related but it feels like they area.  I will get dizzy randomly several times throughout the day.  Pain in my calves, shins, and thighs.  Migraine headaches.  Randomly it will become very hard to breathe and I will be unable to take breathe.  Overall fatigue, tiredness, and just feeling unwell.

I have been to the both the ER and regular doctors office close to 15 times since this started.  I have had all kinds of tests run and they come back clean within normal range.  I was told by the doctors that since I am young and not at risk for anything with my heart that they can't really do a whole lot for me.  The most I was able to get was a holter monitor for 2 weeks.  I have the results of all of the tests blood, urine, xrays, the holter monitor.  If you have any questions about the tests please let me know and I will do my best to answer.  

  
Any help is appreciated.  Thank you in advance.
